title: UniBOM: A Unified SBOM Analysis and Visualisation Tool for IoT Systems and Beyond
local_full_text: ressources/papers/UniBOM - Unified Software Bill of Materials.pdf
objective: Integrate binary, filesystem, and source analysis with SBOM generation, vulnerability analysis, comparison, and visualization for IoT systems.
method: A Node.js workflow integrates Binwalk, Syft, Grype, and CCScanner, then presents component, CVE, comparison, history, and memory-safety views through a web interface.
ground_truth_and_dataset: The evaluation uses 258 Linux-based wireless gateway firmware images and source analyses of four IoT operating-system codebases. It compares generated vulnerability counts across tools but does not establish a complete component-level ground truth.
transformation_scope: Firmware extraction and non-package-managed C/C++ recovery are considered; Android R8, DEX module decoupling, and adjacent Maven-version discrimination are outside scope.
metrics_and_results: The paper reports comparative component and vulnerability findings rather than precision, recall, or exact-version accuracy against a complete gold standard.
artifact_availability: UniBOM is presented as an open-source tool.
uncertainty_and_limitations: The evaluation is demonstration-oriented and lacks complete component-level ground truth.
Higher vulnerability counts do not by themselves prove higher precision.
The study is adjacent SBOM evidence and cannot support Android Maven exact-version claims.
sbom_relevance: Supports end-to-end integration of multiple evidence sources, SBOM comparison, and downstream vulnerability visualization while illustrating the need to separate workflow breadth from attribution accuracy.
